description: Validates connection pool configurations for positive numeric limits, client connection headroom, host reference declarations, recognised auth/TLS modes, and failover policy

rules.description: connection-pool-spec.json must exist, be valid JSON, and declare pooler, maxClientConn, poolSize, and host
maxClientConn, poolSize, and maxConnections (when declared) must be positive integers. Non-positive or non-integer values are rejected by PgBouncer/pgpool at startup with a configuration parse error

maxClientConn must be >= poolSize. If maxClientConn < poolSize, the pool exhausts available connections immediately. Additionally, headroom below 10% of maxClientConn causes queueing under normal load spikes (overridable with skipHeadroomCheck: true)
rules.note: Skipped when maxClientConn or poolSize is absent

constraints.maxClientConn >= poolSize: Required — otherwise pool is immediately saturated
constraints.headroom >= 10%: Advisory — less than 10% headroom causes load-spike queueing

rules.description: authType and tlsMode, when declared, must use recognised values. An unrecognised authType causes PgBouncer to reject the config at startup. An invalid tlsMode silently falls back to the default, which may be weaker than intended
rules.note: Skipped for fields that are absent

rules.description: The host field must reference a hostname or env var rather than a literal IP address. Literal IPs in connection pool configs are fragile — they break on DB primary failover
connection-pool-spec.json must not contain TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, or PLACEHOLDER markers
TLS must not be disabled (tlsMode: disable) without a disableTlsJustification. A failoverPolicy must be declared to handle DB primary failover without manual pool restart

constraints.tls-disable: tlsMode: 'disable' requires disableTlsJustification to be set
